clauses.reason: The operative paragraph reads "I hereby exempt the said Harry Peale from compulsory retirement for age for a period of six months ending July 31, 1939." The exemption is a one-time permission for a fixed period and the period is stated in the order itself. By its own terms it runs through July 31, 1939, recorded inclusive under research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md; the exclusive reading ends it when July 31, 1939 begins. State on 2026-10-14: terminated, the permission having been exhausted by lapse of the stated period.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 8002 of November 7, 1938, signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt, exempts Harry Peale from compulsory retirement for age for a period of six months ending July 31, 1939, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a). The held text is the American Presidency Project web transcription (APP node 362925, Wayback Machine capture 2023-09-06T11:18:42Z); its page record in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl names Executive Order 8002, the date agrees with the text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file. The order is one whereas paragraph and one operative paragraph, so it is one clause. The exemption ends by its own terms on July 31, 1939; per research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md that day is recorded as the inclusive end, and the exclusive reading (the exemption stops when that day begins) is the alternative a reviewer should see. The OFR catalog search and the held-text name search both report zero hits for this order, so no revoking, superseding or extending instrument is recorded in the packet.

One clause covers the whole order; the clause span in the dossier is the full text from the whereas paragraph through the signature block."}

savings.reason: The order grants a permission for a fixed period and contains no saving or transfer provision. What it left behind, Harry Peale's continued federal employment during the period, accrued while the period ran; no duty or right continues after July 31, 1939 by the order's own terms.
